L20·N747unmasked layer
Fires weakly-to-moderately on small connective/function tokens ("of", "and", "the", "(", "-west") that link parts of a compound technical name or phrase, and is strongly suppressed by the parallel connectives that introduce a geographic location after an institution name ("in Boston", ", Switzerland", "Medical Center at…").

L23·N11224unmasked layer
Fires on connector/boundary tokens (commas, dashes, newlines, prepositions like "for", or the head noun) that sit immediately before a continuation naming a specific entity or added detail (e.g. "artist, Christian Tamburr", "diver- Samir Kapoor", "Los Angeles Air Force Base"), i.e. a mid-sentence hand-off point into an appositive/proper-noun expansion, rather than any single lexical item.

L28·N11120unmasked layer
Fires on characters in the middle of opaque alphanumeric identifier strings — hex color codes, bit.ly/tinyurl slugs, survey/section codes — with the strongest (negative) response on continuation characters of other codes like UK postcodes, VINs and radio call signs, i.e. it is a "next character of an arbitrary code string" detector rather than a semantic one.
